title: Fix survivors SFX volume balance vs audio tracker tracks
description:
The sound effects in the survivors game are 3-4x quieter than the audio tracker song playback. When background music tracks are added to survivors, the SFX will be drowned out.

Current state in engine.js:
- masterGain: 0.4
- SFX note volumes: 0.08-0.15
- SFX noise volumes: 0.1
- Ambient gain: 0.06

Need to either boost SFX volumes or add a separate music gain node that can be mixed lower relative to SFX. A dedicated music bus at ~0.25x the SFX level would let background tracks play without overwhelming gameplay sounds.
design: Add a musicGain node in the Audio module (engine.js) separate from the SFX path. Route background music through musicGain with a lower default (e.g. 0.1-0.15) while keeping SFX routed through the existing masterGain at 0.4. This gives independent volume control for music vs SFX.
acceptance_criteria:
- Background music plays at a level that does not overpower SFX
- SFX (weapon sounds, hit sounds, pickup sounds) remain clearly audible over music
- Volume balance feels natural during gameplay
- Music gain can be adjusted independently of SFX
notes:
## Retro
- What worked: Clear task spec made implementation straightforward. Adding a parallel gain bus without touching existing SFX routing was clean.
- What was unclear: Nothing significant - the task was well-defined.

title: Keyboard Guitar Hero — rhythm game using the sheet music renderer
description:
Build a Guitar Hero-style rhythm game where notes scroll toward a fixed playhead and the player hits keyboard keys to score points. The sheet music visualizer renderer already implements 90% of the visual mechanic.

## Concept

Notes scroll right-to-left on a grand staff, approaching a glowing cursor line. The player presses keys when notes cross the cursor to score hits. Accuracy windows (perfect/great/good/miss) determine points and combo multipliers. Could live in `games/` or as a mode within the visualizer.

## Existing Infrastructure

### Sheet Music Renderer (`music/visualizer/renderers/sheet-music.js`)
- Scrolling grand staff with treble + bass clefs
- Notes color-coded by channel (gold/rose/purple/silver → 4 lanes)
- Duration beams showing note length
- Glowing playhead at 15% from left edge
- Binary-search indexed timeline for efficient visible-note lookup
- `findFirst(rowThreshold)` already finds notes near the cursor
- Notes have `atCursor` detection (row <= currentRowFrac && noteEnd > currentRowFrac)

### Visualizer Engine (`music/visualizer/engine.js`)
- `frameData.cursor.totalFracRow` — precise fractional scroll position
- `frameData.analysis.timeline[row][ch]` — all note data pre-analyzed
- `frameData.analysis.channelRoles` — lead/harmony/bass/percussion per channel
- `frameData.currentNotes[ch]` — what's playing right now
- `frameData.analysis.rpb` — rows per beat for timing windows
- Song library of 57 songs at various difficulties

### Music Video Integration
The visualizer's music videos (`music/visualizer/music-videos/`) are self-contained HTML pages that load engine.js + playback-engine.js. A Guitar Hero mode could overlay on any video as a secondary canvas/UI, or be a standalone renderer. Frame callbacks (`Visualizer.addFrameCallback`) let secondary renderers subscribe to the same timing data.

## Design Considerations

- **Input mapping**: 4 channels → 4 keys (e.g., D/F/J/K or similar). Each channel is already color-coded.
- **Hit detection**: Compare key press time against note arrival at cursor. Use `analysis.secondsPerRow` to convert row distance to timing windows.
- **Scoring**: Perfect/Great/Good/Miss windows, combo multiplier, streak counter.
- **Visual feedback**: Note glow/flash on hit, miss animation, combo counter display, score overlay.
- **Difficulty**: Song BPM + note density naturally creates difficulty tiers. The song manifest has BPM data. Could auto-rate songs.
- **"Through the Fire and Flames" is the boss level**: High BPM + dense 4-channel patterns = maximum difficulty.
- **Could work as**: (a) a new visualizer renderer with input handling, (b) a standalone game page in `games/`, or (c) an overlay mode on music videos.

## Tech Notes

- Vanilla JS only, no frameworks (project rule)
- The sheet music renderer is an IIFE on `window.Renderers` — could fork it or extend it with a game layer
- `KeyboardEvent` listeners for input, `performance.now()` or `AudioContext.currentTime` for precise timing
- Consider mobile tap zones for touchscreen play (the project runs on GitHub Pages, mobile-friendly is a plus)
close_reason: Built full Rhythm Hero game at games/rhythm-hero/index.html with sheet-music note highway, 4-key input (D/F/J/K), timing-based scoring, combo system, particle effects, and animated results screen

title: Engine: improve hit model (swept segments, target zones, contact events)
description: Replace the current single-point-vs-torso-center hit detection with swept segment tests for fist/weapon over active hit frames, multiple target zones (head/torso/limbs), and a deterministic contact event payload (point, normal, strength, moveName). This makes hits feel precise and enables contact-driven FX.
notes:
## prepared.prompt

## Context
Current hit detection uses a single point (weapon tip or fist) vs a torso-center radius check. This gives mushy timing and no spatial feedback. For stickdeath-style fights, hits need to feel precise — you should see the fist connect with the head, not just "be near the torso."

## Task
Improve the hit detection system in `stick-fight-engine.js`.

### Requirements
1. **Swept segment test** - Instead of a point-vs-radius check, test the attacking limb segment (e.g., elbow→hand for punches, hand→swordTip for slashes) against target body segments. Use segment-vs-segment closest-point distance.
2. **Multiple target zones** - Define hit zones on the target:
   - `head`: neck→head segment + head radius
   - `torso`: hip→neck segment
   - `armL`/`armR`: shoulder→elbow→hand chains
   - `legL`/`legR`: hip→knee→ankle chains
   Each zone can have a damage multiplier (head: 1.5x, limbs: 0.7x).
3. **Contact event payload** - When a hit connects, return/emit a contact event object:
   ```
   { point: {x, y},           // world-space contact point
     normal: {x, y},          // impact direction (normalized)
     strength: 0-1,           // based on attack progress (peak at hitAt timing)
     moveName: 'punch_r',     // which move connected
     zone: 'head',            // which target zone was hit
   ```

1. **Gait phase** - Track a `gaitPhase` (0-1 cycle) on each figure, driven by `abs(velocity)`. Phase advances proportional to distance traveled per frame.

5. **Shoulder counter-rotation** - Shoulders twist opposite to pelvis (natural walking motion). Add a `shoulderTwist` derived value that offsets shoulderL/shoulderR y-positions slightly.

### Implementation approach
- Add `fig.velocity` tracking (computed from frame-to-frame `fig.x` delta in `updateFigure`)
- Add `fig.gaitPhase`, `fig.lastX`, `fig.plantFootL`, `fig.plantFootR` state
- In `updateFigure`, before the lerp loop: if `abs(velocity) > threshold`, advance gait and override leg/hip targets
- The locomotion should blend smoothly with posed motion (when velocity is near zero, gait influence fades out)
- Expose `fig.velocity` so videos can read it

- All existing video files must work without changes

title: Improve StickFight motion and battle direction for StickDeath-style videos
description:
## Context
Goal is an early-2000s stickdeath.com style fight engine used across music videos, but current limb motion feels awkward and battle scenes feel bland.

## What I reviewed
- `music/visualizer/stick-fight-engine.js`
- `music/visualizer/fencing-match-in-a-thunderstorm-video.html`
- `music/visualizer/tavern-brawl-crescendo-video.html`
- `music/visualizer/through-the-fire-and-flames-video.html`
- `music/visualizer/system-infection-video.html`

## Core problems found
1. Battle choreography often bypasses combat API.
- Some battle videos mainly drive `setPose`/`setTarget` and do not use `StickFight.attack()` + hit resolution, so combat reads as pantomime.

2. Contact and impact are not event-accurate.
- Clash sparks/flashes are frequently spawned from fixed scene points or beat events rather than actual weapon/limb contact.

3. Motion model is too limited for believable limbs.
- Engine has no foot planting, pelvis/torso twist, or gait solver; mostly lean/bounce/knee/arm parameters.

4. Hit detection is coarse.
- One-point strike vs torso-center radius gives mushy hit timing and weak impact readability.

5. Handedness/stance assumptions are rigid.
- Weapon logic is effectively left-hand centric and can look wrong depending on facing/pose.

6. One major section-timing bug in TTFAF finale.
- Finale kill trigger uses a beat threshold that is larger than the effective finale section duration, so the intended climax can fail to fire.

## Recommendations (prioritized)
### P1 Engine upgrades (highest leverage)
1. Add locomotion layer:
- gait phase driven by velocity
- foot-plant windows with anti-slide
- pelvis sway + shoulder counter-rotation

2. Add richer kinematic controls:
- torso twist, hip shift, head tilt/bob
- optional per-limb phase offsets

3. Improve hit model:
- swept segment tests for fist/weapon over active hit frames
- multiple target zones (head/torso/limbs)
- deterministic contact event payload (`point`, `normal`, `strength`, `moveName`)

4. Add stance/handedness model:
- `weaponHand`, `leadSide`, mirror-safe attack definitions

### P2 Battle direction system
1. Build a choreography layer per section:
- scripted attack/counter/recovery chains
- intentional whiffs and spacing beats
- reduced random move spam

2. Build a camera/director layer:
- hit-stop (2-3 frames)
